context.zh: 臨終，枕帝膝曰：「叔父駿女男胤有德色，願陛下以備六宮。」
context.idiomatic: Dying with her head on his knee she said, “My uncle Yang Jun’s daughter Nanyin combines virtue and beauty—please bring her into the six palaces.”
context.literal: At the end, pillowing on the emperor’s knee she said: “Uncle Yang Jun’s niece has virtue and beauty; I beg Your Majesty to keep her for the six palaces.”

context.zh: 武悼楊皇后諱芷，字季蘭，小字男胤，元后從妹。
context.idiomatic: Empress Yang Wudao—personal name Zhi, courtesy Jilan, pet name Nanyin—was cousin to the founding empress.
context.literal: Empress Yang Wudao, taboo name Zhi, courtesy name Jilan, childhood name Nanyin, was a younger cousin of Empress Yuan.

context.zh: 又見故尚書僕射裴頠議悼后故事，稱繼母雖出，追服無改。
context.idiomatic: The late Vice Director Pei Wei, discussing the precedent of the Mourned Empress, held that mourning for a stepmother continues even after she is cast out.
context.literal: I also saw former Minister Director Pei Yi’s opinion on Empress Dao’s case—though a stepmother had departed, mourning obligations stayed unchanged.

context.zh: 昔有莘適殷，姜姒歸周，宣德中闈，徽音永流。
context.idiomatic: Youxin wed Yin; Jiang and Si married into Zhou—inner chambers rang with virtue.
context.literal: Ancient Youxin married Yin; Jiang Si returned to Zhou—virtue spread within the palace, fair fame forever flows.

context.zh: 芳曰：「死且不畏，何畏陛下！」
context.idiomatic: She shot back, “I do not fear even death—why should I fear Your Majesty?”
context.literal: Fang said: “I fear not death—why fear His Majesty!”

context.zh: 武帝慮太子尚幼，未知帷房之事，乃遣往東宮侍寢，由是得幸有身。
context.idiomatic: Wu, worried the crown prince was still young and did not know the affairs of the bedchamber, sent her to the Eastern Palace to attend him in bed—she conceived.
context.literal: Emperor Wu worried crown prince still young—did not know inner chamber affairs—therefor dispatched go Eastern Palace attend bedding—thereby gained favor pregnant.
